messages:
esther: Quick sync— ran a focused AB on reranker-v2 (PTQ int8) comparing two input treatments: (A) raw query, (B) short prefix 'Q:' + query (we call it 'sentinel-prefix'). Seeing ndcg up on knowledge corpora but mrr down on support traces.

ben: Can you drop the numbers and which holdout?

esther: Holdout: 2026-03-14 stratified-by-intent, sample=6k. seed=2026. Summary below.

omar: table paste:

```
catalog   | arm           | ndcg@10 | mrr
----------|---------------|---------|-----
kb        | raw           | 0.729   | 0.476
kb        | sentinel      | 0.739   | 0.471
support   | raw           | 0.667   | 0.404
support   | sentinel      | 0.654   | 0.389
```

ben: interesting. so ndcg improves on kb but mrr drops on support. any diagnostics?

esther: dug into per-query deltas. two dominant failure modes for support: (1) token-merge at start of short queries when prefix attaches to first token, increasing subword splits; (2) many support docs have inline HTML/markup causing different candidate text boundaries which when combined with tokenization shift produces tie flips.

omar: can you show an example token diff?

esther: example (raw vs sentinel):
```
raw:  ["how", "to", "reset"] -> tokens: [how, to, re##set]
sentinel: ["Q:", "how", "to", "reset"] -> tokens: [Q, :, ho##w, to, re##set]
```
Result: first token now ho##w (different split) -> embedding/attention context shift -> top2 score gap shrinks from 6e-3 to 2e-4 -> ordering flips after PTQ quantization.

ben: PTQ noise makes sense as amplifier. did you try a punctuation-safe sentinel like 'Query:\n'? that might avoid merging.

esther: yes, I prototyped 'Query:\n' and a sentinel that ends with a space + newline. early micro-run: support MRR loss reduced by ~30% vs 'Q:' sentinel but still not zero.

omar: what about stripping formatting from candidate docs? strip-html might reduce noise.

esther: I ran a small paired run with --strip-html and saw support mrr loss vanish (within noise). kb still benefits from sentinel. So hypothesis: sentinel helps ambiguous kb queries but hurts when doc formatting/HTML interacts with tokenizer.

ben: action items?

esther: plan: 
- run comprehensive paired AB (n=50k) with three arms: raw, Q: sentinel, punctuation-safe sentinel.
- run same arms with --strip-html true to quantify doc-format effect.
- re-run PTQ calibration with seeds [1, 13, 99] to measure quant instability (emit quant-score-variance).
- add deterministic tie-breaker flag (ranker.fallback=doc_id) in eval to measure tie_rate delta without changing production ordering.
- produce per-slice effect matrix (slice keys: corpus, query_len_bin, html_noise_bin, tie_rate).

omar: please include eval command you used earlier so we can reproduce.

esther: command copy: 
```
./tools/eval_rerank \
  --model models/reranker-v2-int8.ptq \
  --holdout s3://bench/holdouts/2026-03-14.json \
  --priming templates/sentinel-q.json \
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 2026 --samples 6000 \
  --emit-token-diff --out s3://bench/artifacts/6801234567_ab.json
```
bench-bot: Job 6801234568 queued: eval_rerank (arms=raw,sentinel,punct-safe; samples=6000).

ben: also add a small calibration-only eval where you compute score distributions per-token-length to see where quantization is most sensitive. Could help us craft a quant-aware priming (e.g., shorter sentinel).

esther: noted. I'll add a tiny calibration run and include an 'effective-token-shift' metric (mean token index of first subword change).

omar: long-term options: corpus-aware input routing (enable sentinel for kb routes, disable for support), or run a lightweight prefix-normalizer that inserts a zero-width space between sentinel and query to prevent merges. Both are doable.

esther: yes. after the full runs we'll compute the effect matrix and then decide: (A) enable sentinel via routing, (B) use punctuation-safe sentinel globally, or (C) disable and explore model-side priming embedding.

ben: sweet. tag me when artifacts land. thanks for the triage. :thumbsup:
